changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: For retailers with stores and a website, and for the operations executive who owns the stores: "One system for the tills and the website: one customer, one basket. Buy online, return in store, and the till sees the order, refunds it and updates the same customer and loyalty record." Back the line with a live demo of an online order returned at a store till, step by step, with the refund and the customer record on screen. Drop "unified commerce" and "point of sale" from customer-facing copy for this buyer.
changes.why: The customer dismissed our M3 line as "that's a diagram", asked to watch a live till return that we only described, and described what they wanted as "one system for the tills and the website" and "one customer, one basket", never "unified commerce".

changes.change: For store rollouts, aimed at the COO or store operations lead: "One vendor accountable from install to go-live. You won't have two vendors pointing at each other." Name the rollout owner and the people who have run store rollouts, say who installs the tills, explain what happens to the old tills, and state the on-call coverage, all in a rollout plan with dates.
changes.why: The buyer's stated fear was "two vendors pointing at each other". Our "we'd bring in a partner" answer to who installs ended the store ops workshop, and the buyer asked for a rollout plan with dates, installers and old-till handling, while Adyen brought a retail team and one contract.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: For retail buyers with stores and online: "Talk to retailers who run their tills and website on us," backed by a standing roster of store-and-online retail references who can take a call within days, chosen where possible from names the buyer already knows.
changes.why: The customer asked "can I talk to them?" and we couldn't arrange a call in time, while Adyen named retailers the COO already knew.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: Don't open with global infrastructure for store-led retailers. Open with the store-floor moment instead: "A customer bought online and came back to return it in store, and the till couldn't see the order." Follow it with the broken loyalty record, then the one-system answer.
changes.why: The deal was triggered by a returns queue the COO watched in a store, where the till couldn't see online orders and loyalty didn't work everywhere, and the evaluation moved from web to stores. Global currency coverage played no part.
